script.title: Why Doctors Found a Stone Baby Carried for 50 Years
sentences: A woman carried a fetus inside her body for fifty years.
Spanish physician Abū al-Qāsim first documented this in the tenth century.
It happens when a fetus dies during an abdominal pregnancy.
To block dangerous infections, the host body builds a protective barrier.
It gradually coats the entire fetus in calcium.
Remarkably, some women later delivered healthy children without incident.
Doctors usually spot the calcified fetus on X-rays after menopause.
Only three hundred cases exist in four hundred years of records.
Her body simply turned a tragedy into stone.
script.description:
The strange medical history of lithopedion, or stone babies.
How the human body calcifies a fetus to protect the host.
claims_en: A woman carried a lithopedion for fifty years before diagnosis.
Spanish physician Abū al-Qāsim first described lithopedion in the 10th century.
Lithopedion occurs when a fetus dies during an abdominal pregnancy.
The body calcifies the fetus as a foreign body reaction to prevent septic infection.
Women with lithopedia have later given birth to healthy children without incident.
Lithopedia are often discovered during X-ray examinations well after menopause.
There are only 300 known cases of lithopedion recorded in 400 years of medical literature.
